chunks: Would you call on Baal and leave the best of creators,

key_terms.أَحْسَنَ الْخَالِقِينَ: The best of creators, a title referring to Allah as the supreme and most excellent creator
key_terms.بَعْلًا: Baal, a title meaning 'lord' or 'master', often referring to a specific pagan deity or chief god in pre-Islamic Arabia

ai.seo_question: Why are polytheists criticized for worshipping Baal instead of Allah?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah As-Saffat, this verse critiques the polytheists' irrational preference for Baal—a title often associated with rain gods or chief deities in pre-Islamic Arabia—over Allah, the ultimate Architect of existence. Shia exegetes emphasize the contrast between the static, created nature of idols and the dynamic, creative power of the Divine, underscoring the logical fallacy of worshipping the created while neglecting the Creator. This rhetorical question serves as a foundational argument for Tawhid, challenging the cognitive dissonance of idolaters who recognize Allah's power in creation but fail to direct their worship to Him alone.
